problem: The HomeRobot OVMM heuristic baseline fails often: it misclassifies objects and receptacles (including the floor), oscillates between adjacent states, ignores collisions in replanning, loses the object from view when picking, and places imprecisely or blindly.
motivation: Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation in unseen homes needs reliable perception, navigation, picking and placing. An exhaustive evaluation of the baseline showed specific, fixable deficiencies in each skill, and perception errors were the main root cause of failed episodes.
key_idea: Keep the modular heuristic HomeRobot agent and fix its failure modes in each skill with targeted heuristics: per-class detection thresholds, a floor filter, goal-versus-frontier choice, probability-weighted receptacle selection, picking retries and success checks, and safer placing.
insight: Most failures in a modular pipeline come from perception and simple planning pathologies, so targeted heuristics give sizable partial-success gains (10.5% to 18.6%). The authors state that refining perception had the largest impact, and that recognition of objects and receptacles remains the main bottleneck. No per-component ablation table is given, so this is a qualitative claim.
method: Detection: per-class dynamic confidence thresholds for Detic, plus a depth-based height threshold that removes floor-level receptacle detections (false positives).

Exploration: a decision mechanism on the goal map lets the agent choose between the goal point and frontier exploration, avoiding infinite oscillation. Receptacle detection probabilities are stored in the BEV map and the reachable receptacle with the highest match probability is chosen.
Navigation: detected collisions are written into the obstacle map at the last short-term goal so replanning changes. Goals aim for the center of the receptacle, which gives better placing poses.
Picking: if the first pick fails the agent rotates left and right to widen its view. A pick-success check is added, and on failure the agent returns to navigation and searches other locations.

Placing: approach the receptacle in small steps over several iterations, and move the placing point away from receptacle edges. If the receptacle is no longer detected, place on any surface, and drop large objects from a greater height.
State machine: six states (Find object, Navigate to object, Pick, Find end receptacle, Navigate to end receptacle, Place), with Detic segmentation and depth-based semantic BEV mapping.

setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + pose + joint states, Detic segmentation, semantic BEV map
setting.action_space: low-level base motion with high-level pick/place skill commands (Stretch robot)

numbers.evidence: Table 1: Evaluation results of the top three agents over the 1000 episodes of the Test Standard Phase; UniTeam 2% / 18.6% / 1140.54

results: On the OVMM Test Standard phase, UniTeam reaches 2% overall success and 18.6% partial success, against 0% and 10.5% for the heuristic baseline. It ties PieSquare on overall success (2%) with much higher partial success (11.1%), and trails KuzHum (2.8% / 19.1%).
limitations: Overall success is very low (2%), and there is no ablation quantifying each fix
Recognition of objects and receptacles remains the main bottleneck, with further failures from narrow passages, oversized receptacles and placing through walls
Heuristic fixes are hand-tuned; the Recognize-Anything prompt filtering did not help; simulation only
